short_description: There are incentives to reduce life cycle greenhouse gas emissions both in the area of new building promotion and in the area of investment promotion (small and large-volume residential construction). measure_name: BauPolG - §37a Charging and Network Infrastructure
short_description: (1) For the construction of buildings with a parking space requirement of more than 10 mandatory parking spaces, the following facilities of the La deInfrastruktur shall be established: 1. in the case of residential buildings, the pipeline infrastructure for each mandatory parking space; 2. in the case of non-residential buildings, a recharging point and, for every fifth starting mandatory parking space, the line infrastructure. In the case of mixed-use buildings, the requirements of points 1 and 2 only apply if the respective use (residential or non-residential use) is accompanied by a parking space requirement of more than 10 parking spaces. The provincial government may adopt more detailed provisions with regard to the technical requirements for recharging points and pipeline infrastructure by means of a regulation. (2) In the case of existing buildings, facilities of the required infrastructure shall be retrofitted in accordance with subsection (1) if structural measures for renovation or renewal or conversion are carried out, which also cover the mandatory parking spaces or the electrical engineering infrastructure of the construction. (3)In the case of existing non-residential buildings or mixed-use buildings with a parking space requirement of more than 20 parking spaces (for non-residential use), a charging point shall in any case be retrofitted by 1 January 2024. (4)When constructing construction facilities or renewing the electrically- technical infrastructure of existing construction facilities, appropriate precautions (e.g. empty piping) must be taken to ensure that the construction facilities can be equipped with an access point for electronic communication and with high-speed-capable in-building physical infrastructure up to the network termination points.

This goal is achieved, on the one hand, by expanding renewable energies and, on the other hand, by consistently reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Both the expansion of renewable energy production and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions will continue beyond 2030. Burgenland pursues the goal of phasing out fossil fuels (oil, gas, coal) by 2040 and takes the necessary measures within the scope of its competences. Maintain and continue to drive forward the pioneering role in the expansion of renewable energies. The heat price cap is a subsidy of the country for Bur Genoese private households. The support is intended to help households with low and middle incomes to cope with the enormous increase in heating costs. When calculating the level of support of the heat price cap, the net household income and the heat cost (heating costs) of the household are taken into account. The heat price cap is a promotion of the state for Burgenland private house think. The support is intended to help households with small and medium-sized incomes to cope with the enormous increase in heating costs. When calculating the subsidy amount of the heat price cap, the net household income and the heating costs (heating costs) of the house are taken into account.

quantified_objective: The aim of the Bgld Climate Protection Laws and the Climate Strategy 2030 is to achieve climate and energy neutrality in the balance sheet by 2030 and to phase out the use of fossil fuels by 2040. Further expansion of new bare energies. To produce at least 9 300 GWh of renewable energy in 2030. Burgenland aims to supply households and companies with renewable energy as cost-effectively and safely as possible, for example by expanding the association ‘Fanclub Burgenland Energieindependent’ or supporting renewable energy communities. Support for the costs of room heating for Burgenland households with small and medium incomes through the heat price cap.

measure_name: Climate-neutral administration Styria
short_description: Improvement of buildings owned by public bodies, including policies and measures in accordance with Articles 5, 6 and 7 of Directive (EU) 2023/1791
quantified_objective: Under the project ‘ELENA (European Local Energy Assistance) StyriA’, an investment programme worth EUR 52.9 million is being implemented by the project partners Land Steiermark, LIG and Stadt Graz under the consortium management of the Styrian Energy Agency. This includes comprehensive energy efficiency measures in public buildings, the construction of building-based PV systems and the installation of charging stations for electric vehicles, with the aim of making a significant contribution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption. The objectives of the investment programme are to achieve total annual energy savings of 11 GWh, in particular through thermal renovations and conversion of lighting to LEDs, which corresponds to a reduction of approximately 50% compared to the baseline, and the installation of 13 GWh of renewable energies. This results in a total annual reduction of approximately 4,600 tonnes of CO2 equivalents, representing a reduction of 87% from baseline.

estimated_impact: • Reduction of energy consumption • Improving energy efficiency

short_description: The Climate and Energy Strategy Styria 2030 plus sees itself as a contribution of Styria to the internationally agreed targets in the climate and energy sector. The strategy forms the basis for an innovative, sustainable, affordable future in the fields of climate protection, climate change adaptation, energy efficiency, renewable energy and energy supply in Styria. estimated_impact: Achieving Styria's energy and climate targets by 2030, 2040 and beyond • TREIBHAUSGASEMISSIONS -48% by 2030 • TOTAL ENERGY CONSUMPTION -17% by 2030 • Share of RENEWABLE ENERGY 55% by 2030 • Share of RENEWABLE STATE 65% by 2030
state_of_implementation: The Styria Climate and Energy Strategy has a history that builds on previous climate protection plans and energy strategies. A major milestone was the merging of these parallel concepts into the Climate and Energy Strategy Styria (KESS), which was decided in 2019 to bundle the targets for greenhouse gas reduction, energy efficiency and renewable energies. It was replaced by the new KESS 2030+ strategy, which was presented in 2024 and aims at climate neutrality of the Land administration by 2030. An action plan has been developed to accompany the implementation of the climate and energy strategy. The first action plan 2019-2021 was adopted on 8 August 2019 and concluded at the end of 2021. Following the completion of the second action plan period at the end of 2024, the third three-year action plan 2025-2027, adopted on 3 July 2025, is currently in force. Similar to the strategy document, the 89 measures of the action plan 2025-2027 are divided into seven areas of impact and build on the directions defined therein.

short_description: Benefits of the Municipal Energy Plan for municipalities in the context of EED III (Articles 5 and 6) The Energy Efficiency Directive (EED III) requires municipalities to implement measures to improve energy efficiency. A structured energy concept specifically supports municipalities in complying with these regulations and at the same time brings environmental and economic advantages. 1. Public bodies must reduce their energy consumption by at least 1.9% per year (Article 5) 2. As of October 2025, at least 3% of heated/cooled public buildings >250m ² must be refurbished to nearly zero-energy buildings per year (Article 6) The energy concept helps by: a) Systematic recording and analysis of the energy consumption of public buildings using software; b) Identification of recovery needs and prioritisation of efficiency measures; c) increase energy savings through targeted optimisation and modernisation; d) Compliance with the recovery rate by planning and documenting measures in cash; e) integration of renewable energies to reduce reliance on fossil fuels; f) Transparent reporting to meet legal requirements wisely. A holistic energy concept makes it easier for municipalities to implement the EED III Directive by enabling structured planning, optimisation and control of energy-saving measures. As a result, not only legal requirements are met, but also long-term cost savings and sustainability goals are achieved.

In implementation of Article 7(2) and Annex III of Directive (EU) 2024/1275, the Austrian Institute of Civil Engineering (OIB) is preparing the OIB Directive 7 ‘Sustainable use of natural resources’ with an expected date of issue in 2027, which is intended to regulate the requirements for the calculation of the life cycle GWP. In the OIB Directive 7, the classification, the calculation method and the use of the underlying data are to be regulated, whereby it is provided that a generic data basis is provided by the OIB, which can be used to calculate the life cycle greenhouse potential. measure_name: Renewable Heat Act, Steiermärkisches Baugesetz, Steier märkisches Raumordnungsgesetz
short_description: Renewable heat law The Renewable Heat Act (EWG) in Austria prohibits the construction of fossil heating systems in Neubauten and requires the use of renewable energies or quality-assured district heating. District heating shall be deemed to be quality assured if at least 80 % of it comes from renewable energies, combined heat and power plants, waste heat or a combination thereof. There is still no general obligation for existing farms, but the conversion is supported by subsidies. Styrian Building Act (Steiermärkisches Baugesetz) Concretely, in the case of new buildings, installations for the provision of heat must not contradict the requirements of the EEC. The same applies to buildings that are conditioned by changes in use. The use of high- efficiency alternative systems must be tested before replacing existing heat supply systems that can be operated with fossil fuels. Section 6 regulates the obligation to connect district heating (to a highly efficient district heating system) in the case of new buildings. Styrian Spatial Planning Act The subject area concept Energy (SKE) is a binding part of the local development concepts in Styria and serves the energy space planning at the municipal level. Its goal is to shape a sustainable energy and climate future by linking energy and climate policy objectives with spatial development. It analyses the energy state of a community and develops strategies for the efficient use of space, such as for renewable energy supply and mobility, and serves as a basis for binding definitions in the local development concept.

measure_name: TIROL 2050 energy-autonomous; consulting services of the Energy Agency Tyrol
short_description: TIROL 2050 energy-autonomous is the central energy policy objective of the Tyrolean state government, which was last confirmed as part of the "Life with a future: Tyrolean sustainability and climate strategy 2025- 2027"programme of measures. TIROL 2050 energy-autonomous stands for a livable and crisis-proof future for the next gene ratios – free of fossil fuels. On the way there, implementation support is needed, because not only technologies such as photovoltaics or e-mobility will play a role. The transition to a sustainable society is best achieved through many individual steps and the diversity of ideas of the people in Tyrol. Concrete activities and measures will therefore be bundled under the umbrella of TIROL 2050 in an energy-autonomous manner and effectively prepared for the public in order to make progress visible and encourage participation. The Energy Agency Tyrol, as the independent regional advisory body on energy issues, combines the necessary fields of expertise and manages this nationwide change process with the involvement of the most important stakeholders.

quantified_objective: Practical assistance in the implementation of measures and projects. At the core of TIROL 2050 energy-autonomous is to reduce energy consumption and expand renewable energies. In order to achieve energy autonomy, the energy consumption in Tyrol must be reduced by 30 percent and fully covered by renewable, domestic energy sources. The Province of Tyrol has commissioned a project team consisting of the Energy Agency Tyrol, the University of Innsbruck and the MCI to develop a target scenario for 2050. The current technology and resource use scenario outlines with which technologies and which domestic resources the energy transition will succeed with continued economic and population growth.

short_description: Energy Promotion Directive 2025 Thermal solar installations on residential buildings are supported with one-off subsidies as part of energy promotion. Implemented on state buildings In the Zero V mission, the expansion of photovoltaic systems was also promoted with the aim of point 2(d): 2. to reduce the energy demand in its own area of activity, i.e. the lane of the building and the vehicle pool, to the highest possible extent by 2040 and to cover it with renewable energy sources ². In order to achieve this objective, it is necessary to adopt an implementation plan for the years 2020 to 2030, which includes the following measures: suitable roof areas of state buildings must be equipped in the best possible way with solar and/or photovoltaic systems, provided that this is prevented by circumstances that cannot be greened (e.g. monument protection, local and landscape image, renovation date, etc.); ² Excluded from the requirement coverage with renewable energy sources are systems for peak load coverage and emergency operation and for vehicles in the areas where no economically justifiable marketable alternative is available (currently e.g. for heavy-duty vehicles, e.g.: riverworks etc.) The Mission Zero V Decision and the 2020-2024 Reports are publicly available and can be found at the following link: https://www.energieautonomie-vorarlberg.at/Focuses/missionze- rov In the summer of 2025, an evaluation of the entire building stock was carried out. The aim was to find further areas for PV systems. Here are the comments on the four groups of buildings according to the previous ta belle: Monument-protected buildings Basically, the Federal Monument Office is now more open to the topic of PV systems on the monument Protected Buildings. However, in the vast majority of cases, this aim is limited by lightning protection. Properties with min 1 building with PV system Here we have been diligent in recent years and have advanced the expansion of the PV systems. Full expansion is likely to be achieved in most cases. Close compression may still be possible in individual cases. No PV system possible or useful For this group of buildings, in our view, the construction of a PV system is either not possible or does not make sense. Buildings to be renovated without PV system This group of buildings still has a refurbishment of the hull in the coming years in accordance with §9 of the "Statute on measures to increase energy efficiency". In the course of the project development for the individual renovations, the installation of a PV system is examined and then, if necessary, implemented with the project hull renovation. Based on the current expansion, a further 300-350 kWp is expected for this sector. Currently, 10 thermal solar systems with 502 m ² are in use.

measure_name: aws Building(s) Tomorrow
short_description: The aim of the aws Building(s) Tomorrow Initiative is to identify and promote Austrian innovation potential in technical development and in the first phases of economic implementation. Measures to raise awareness, network and exchange know-how as well as monetary support are intended to address disruptive innovation opportunities in the building sector in a targeted manner. With this, the aws wants to contribute to the transformation to an economic, ecological and socially fair (more) building sector and to proactively support it.
quantified_objective: The aim of the aws Building(s) Tomorrow funding programme is to highlight the disruptive and innovative potential of Austrian companies and research institutions in the building and construction sector. In particular, companies and research institutions should be encouraged to put disruptive, radical ideas into practice. Specific projects will therefore be funded in the following phases: - Validation of proof-of-concept, - Development and construction of prototypes and - Implementation of pilot and demonstration activities
indicative_budget_and_sources_of_financi: 2024: approx. 2.5 MEUR 2026: approx. 3 MEUR
bodies_responsible_for_implementation: Austria Wirtschaftsservice GmbH (aws)
estimated_impact: a) Radical technical leap Indicators: The project is a leap forward innovation with a high technological risk, especially with regard to the use of new materials, manufacturing processes, high-risk technologies, etc. Measurement Comparative studies, patents, technical specifications, risk analyses. b) Disruption of markets Indicators: Innovation has the potential to appeal to completely new groups of customers or to displace existing market participants. These innovations are rarely more complex than current solutions, but are significantly cheaper to use a smarter, smaller or more convenient. Measurement: market analyses, surveys, interviews, case studies. c) Efficiency and economic impact Indicators: cost savings, revenue growth, new markets, ROI. Measurement: cost savings compared to traditional me thoden, ROI, market share. d) Social and ecological impact Indicators: social infrastructure, environmental impact, jobs. Measurement: Socio-economic analyses, sustainability reports, CO2 balances. The projects must be compatible with the objectives of the European Green Deal and comply with the principle of the Do-No-Significant- Harm.
state_of_implementation: 1. Call for tenders closed 11/25 2. Call for tenders 2026 in preparation

measure_name: climate-active
short_description: klimaaktiv is the climate protection initiative of the Austrian federal government, which supports people, companies and municipalities in implementing climate-friendly measures. It offers expertise, works and a network on topics such as energy saving, renewable energies, energy- efficient construction and sustainable mobility. A significant part is the building standard, which evaluates buildings according to quality, energy efficiency and ecological construction and distinguishes them in three stages (bronze, silver, gold).
type_of_strategy_or_measure: Climate and Energy Strategy Styria 2030 plus Link: https://www.technik.steiermark.at/cms/ziel/128523298/en/
quantified_objective: The main objective of klimaaktiv is to accelerate the market penetration of climate-friendly products and services and thereby reduce greenhouse gas emissions in Austria. The initiative complements legal requirements and funding with the following measures. • Construction and renovation: Support for new buildings and renovations to make buildings more energy-efficient, comfortable and ecological. • Mobility: promoting environmentally friendly mobility through advice and financial incentives for e-mobility, cycling infrastructure and other measures in municipalities. • Renewable energies: advice and support in the use of renewable energy sources. • Energy saving: measures and advice to reduce energy consumption in households, municipalities and companies. Link: https://www.klimaaktiv.at
bodies_responsible_for_implementation: Federal Ministry for Innovation, Mobility and Infrastructure (BMIMI) Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, Climate and Environment Protection, Regions and Water Management (BMLUK) Province of Styria Anchored in areas of housing promotion in Styria. Regional partners:innen - A15 Energie, Wohnbau, Technik represented by Energie Agentur Steiermark
estimated_impact: The goal of climate-active construction is to minimize the negative impact on the climate and make buildings resilient to climate change. This is done by reducing energy and resource consumption as well as greenhouse gas emissions throughout the life of a building, from construction and construction to operation and dismantling. It aims to accelerate the spread of climate-friendly construction methods.

measure_name: ‘Carinthian Building Culture Promotion’ – Building Culture and Municipal Building
short_description: Building culture is visible in buildings, streets, squares as well as in village centers, the cultural landscape or commercial parks. Successful construction culture increases the quality of life, enhances the business location Carinthia and therefore needs attention in planning and implementation. Building culture also aims to ensure that all buildings are appropriately designed to the high quality of our landscape and create added value for our living space.
type_of_strategy_or_measure: In order to establish a promotion in the sense of an increase in quality for architecturally valuable projects, a comprehensive Baukulturförung was created. It is mainly used for municipal project developments (e.g. building construction projects, space design, urban development) in different scales. The technical implementation is based on the agreed building culture guidelines of the state of Carinthia and can thus be aimed at more quality in planning - through suitable processes and structures. The following modules are available in the context of building culture promotion: • Module 1 Project preparation (phase 0, inventories, studies, concepts) • Module 2 Citizen participation, participatory processes • Module 3 Architectural competition
quantified_objective: Depending on requirements and free conveying volume (perpend. 10-15 projects)
indicative_budget_and_sources_of_financi: State and municipal funds (needs allocation outside the framework) The state budget amounts to around € 200,000 per year for 2025 – 2028
bodies_responsible_for_implementation: Department 3 – Sub-Department of Economic Community Supervision and Fund Management
estimated_impact: High-quality planning and implementation of municipal projects and processes.
